title: Accounts Administrator
description:
Accounts Administrator

Overview

We are seeking an organised and detail-oriented Accounts Administrator to support the finance and administration functions of the business. The role covers accounts, payroll, credit control, VAT returns, and general office support. Experience with Sage and a finance or accounting background are essential.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Administration
- Manage supplier, customer and third-party accounts.
- Process bank receipts and deposits.
- Reconcile accounts and investigate discrepancies.
- Raise and process invoices, including proformas and export documentation.
- Carry out credit control, customer statements and payment chasing.
- Manage supplier payments and monthly payment runs.
- Process credit card transactions and maintain accurate VAT records.
- Prepare and submit quarterly VAT returns.
- Maintain accounting records, databases and spreadsheets.
- Set up direct debits, customers and suppliers.
- Assist with year-end accounts and filing.

Payroll Administration
- Maintain employee records within Sage Payroll.
- Process payroll, including overtime, bonuses, deductions and statutory payments.
- Verify employee hours before payroll processing.
- Generate payslips, P45s and annual P60s.
- Process pension and National Insurance contributions.
- Respond to payroll-related queries.
- Onboard new employees onto HR, payroll and pension systems.
- Process leavers and update pension records.
- Assist with payroll year-end and P11 D requirements.
- Ensure employee records remain GDPR compliant.

General Administration
- Answer phones and assist with reception duties.
- Monitor and report staff absences.
- Order PPE, stationery and office supplies.
- Prepare letters and correspondence when required.
- Ensure company certifications and documentation remain up to date.
- Liaise with insurance providers and utility suppliers regarding renewals.
- Support contract renewals and supplier management.
- Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence.
- Undertake ad hoc administrative duties as required.

Skills & Experience

Essential
- Previous experience in an Accounts Administrator or similar finance role.
- Strong bookkeeping and credit control knowledge.
- Sage Accounts and Sage Payroll experience.
- Good Excel and data entry skills.
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Ability to work independently.
- Professional communication and telephone manner.

Desirable
- VAT return preparation experience.
- Payroll administration experience.
- HR administration and employee onboarding experience.
- Experience within manufacturing, engineering or similar sectors.

Personal Attributes
- Reliable and trustworthy.
- Proactive and self-motivated.
- Strong problem-solving skills.
- Able to manage multiple priorities.
- Professional when handling confidential information.
- Flexible team player.

title: Payroll Assistant - Education, Tutoring & Social Work
description:
About the Role

We are a fast-paced recruitment company specialising in the education, tutoring and social work sectors. Due to the high volume of workers we support, we are looking for an organised, accurate and proactive Payroll Assistant to join our busy payroll team.

This is a hands-on role supporting the processing of payroll for a large number of temporary and contract workers. You will work closely with our recruitment and operations teams, managed service vendors and local authorities to ensure hours are received, checked and processed accurately and on time.

The successful candidate will ideally have previous payroll or payroll administration experience and be confident working with large volumes of data. Experience using Merit Payroll Software and/or managed vendor systems for submitting hours to local authorities would be highly advantageous.

This is also a great opportunity for someone who wants to develop their payroll knowledge and, over time, become confident independently running payroll from start to finish.

The Role

You will support the weekly and monthly payroll process, ensuring worker information, bookings, timesheets and hours are accurately recorded and processed within the required deadlines. This will include setting up new workers and bookings, checking timesheets, processing leavers and finishers, maintaining accurate records and assisting with payroll checks and reconciliations before payroll is finalised.

You will work closely with recruitment, operations, managed service providers and local authorities to resolve missing information, discrepancies and payroll queries. You will also respond to queries from workers, consultants and clients in a professional and timely manner, investigate any issues and ensure they are resolved efficiently.

The role will involve working with a high volume of data, producing and checking payroll reports, maintaining up-to-date records and supporting the wider payroll team with general administration and other payroll-related tasks when required.

Payroll Knowledge

You should have a good understanding of payroll principles, or be keen to develop your knowledge in areas including PAYE and income tax, National Insurance, Statutory Sick Pay, Statutory Maternity Pay, holiday pay, starters and leavers, payroll deductions, timesheets and general payroll processes.

You do not need to be an expert in every area from day one, but you should be willing to learn and develop your understanding as you gain experience in the role.

Skills & Experience

Ideally, you will have previous payroll or payroll administration experience, with experience using Merit Payroll Software or a similar payroll system being advantageous. Experience working with managed service providers or submitting hours to local authorities would also be beneficial.

You will need strong Excel and data-entry skills, excellent attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with large volumes of information. You should be organised, comfortable working to tight deadlines and able to prioritise effectively in a busy environment.

Good written and verbal communication skills are essential, as is the ability to investigate and resolve problems proactively. You should be comfortable working independently while also being a strong team player.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who is accurate, reliable, organised and responsive, with a genuine interest in developing their payroll knowledge.

Our payroll environment is busy and high-volume, so you will need to be comfortable working under pressure, meeting deadlines and dealing with a variety of queries throughout the day. Attention to detail is particularly important, as even small errors can have a significant impact on workers' pay.

Most importantly, we are looking for someone who wants to learn and progress. You will initially support the payroll function, but as your knowledge and confidence develop, you will take on increasing responsibility for the overall payroll process.

Development of the Role

The long-term aim is for the successful candidate to become confident in managing payroll independently from start to finish. This will include taking responsibility for setting up new workers and bookings, checking and processing hours, managing starters and finishers, carrying out payroll checks and reconciliations, producing and reviewing payroll reports, resolving payroll queries and discrepancies, and ensuring payroll is completed accurately and on time.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a strong payroll administration background who wants to develop their skills, take on greater responsibility and progress towards becoming a fully independent payroll professional.

description:

- Annual Salary: £27,000 - £31,000 per annum
- Location: Brentwood
- Job Type: Permanent, Full-time - Hybrid (2 days in office, 3 days WFH)

Reed Accountancy are recruiting in Brentwood for a Sales Ledger/Billing & Invoice Specialist. This role is crucial for managing the end-to-end billing cycle, ensuring all materials and subcontractor costs are captured accurately, billed correctly, and recovered in full. This position supports strong commercial performance by protecting margins and providing critical insights through analysis and reporting.

Day-to-day of the role:

title: Temporary Cashier / Credit Controller - Immediate Start
description:
Temporary Cashier / Credit Controller - Immediate start
£15-£18 per hour
Chelmsford, Essex
Monday to Friday, 8am - 4:30pm or 8:30am-5pm - Hybrid

This is a temporary opportunity for around 2 months, with the possibility to be extended. You must be available immediately to be considered for this opportunity.

Role Purpose: To accurately process and allocate customer payments, reconcile bank transactions, investigate unallocated cash, and support the Accounts Receivable function to ensure customer accounts remain accurate and up to date.

Key Responsibilities
- Post and allocate customer receipts onto the accounting system across all companies
- Ensure cash received is accurately matched and allocated against outstanding customer invoices.
- Investigate and resolve unallocated and unidentified cash receipts by liaising with customers and internal teams,
- Daily reconciliation of the bank recs
- Review customer remittances and reconcile complex payment allocations.
- Support the resolution of account queries relating to payments, credits, and outstanding balances.
- Process refunds and adjustments in accordance with company policies and approval procedures.
- Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation for audit purposes.
- Work closely with all teams to resolve payment issues.
- Assist with month-end reporting and reconciliation activities.
- Identify opportunities to improve cash allocation processes and controls.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in an Accounts Receivable, Cashiering, or Finance Administration role.
- Experience of cash allocation and bank reconciliation processes.
- Good understanding of accounting principles and AR procedures.
- Strong attention to detail and high levels of accuracy.
- Excellent problem solving and investigative skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and finance systems
- Ability to manage high transaction volumes and meet deadlines.
- Strong communication skills and ability to liaise with customers and internal departments.

This role is ideal for someone with strong analytical skills who enjoys investigating payment discrepancies and ensuring customer accounts and cash postings are accurate and up to date.
